# Patches to vendored crates

Baseline for each crate is the upstream commit in `UPSTREAM.txt`. Every deviation is listed here with the reason.

## ssh_agent

The socket-path rows are `#[cfg(unix)]` and purely additive: the upstream entry points and their tests are untouched. The `protocol.rs` row fixes behavior; the `clear` and epoch rows are additive public entry points. The review-fix rows below change behavior (zeroization, deadlines, ECDSA session-bind, listener shutdown); where an upstream test had to change, its row says so.

| File | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/server/listener/unix.rs` | `UnixListener::bind(PathBuf)` holds the old body of `new()`; `new()` now calls it with `get_socket_path()`. | Lets the caller choose the socket path without mutating the process-wide `BITWARDEN_SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. |
| `src/server/listener/mod.rs` | New `create_listeners_at(PathBuf)`. | Plumbing for the path. |
| `src/server/mod.rs` | New `SSHAgentServer::start_at_socket_path(PathBuf)`. | Plumbing for the path. |
| `src/agent.rs` | New public `BitwardenSSHAgent::start_at(PathBuf)`. | Entry point used by `crates/ssh`. |
| `src/server/protocol.rs` | `detect_namespace` reads the namespace right after the 6-byte `SSHSIG` magic instead of after magic + a `u32` version. Its unit-test helper `make_sshsig_blob` drops the version field, `detect_namespace_truncated_after_version_returns_unsupported` becomes `..._after_magic_...` with the same intent, and `detect_namespace_reads_the_layout_openssh_signs` is new. | Upstream bug, not Unix-specific: the data an agent signs for `ssh-keygen -Y sign` is `SSHSIG`, namespace, reserved, hash algorithm, hash (`sshsig_wrap_sign` in OpenSSH); the version only exists in the armored signature. With the old offset every real `git`/`file` signature was reported as `Unsupported`, so the approval UI never saw the namespace. Observed with OpenSSH 10.5 in `crates/ssh/tests/agent.rs`. |
| `src/agent.rs` | New public `BitwardenSSHAgent::clear()` calling `KeyStore::clear()` (which resets `initialized`), plus the unit test `clear_clears_the_keystore_without_stopping`. | Upstream only clears on `stop()`, and `replace(vec![])` leaves the keystore `initialized`, so after the first key refresh a list request never reaches `request_list_approval`. vaultkeeper clears on lock / log out / account switch so a locked vault serves no keys and `ssh-add -l` asks the user to unlock. |
| `src/server/listener/windows.rs` | The named pipe is created with `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` and ends with the DACL `D:P(A;;0x12019b;;;<user sid>)(A;;RC;;;OW)`. A pool of 4 instances is created up front with `WRITE_DAC` from the setup DACL `D:P(A;;0x14019f;;;<user sid>)` (the final one denies us `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE` and the owner ACE strips `WRITE_DAC`), the final DACL is applied to every instance with `SetKernelObjectSecurity`, and each instance is recycled after its client disconnects (the recycle first waits up to 2 s for the client to close its end, because `DisconnectNamedPipe` discards data the client has not read yet; then, after `DisconnectNamedPipe`, it clears the stale read/write slot state that mio keeps across `disconnect` — a settle read on the disconnected pipe, a first poll of `connect` so `ConnectNamedPipe` is in flight, and one read that consumes the leftover error — because otherwise the next client's first read receives the previous client's `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE`/`ERROR_PIPE_NOT_CONNECTED`). Every idle instance waits for a client in its own spawned task that hands the connected instance to `accept` through a channel (Windows attaches a client to any listening instance, so awaiting one popped instance left `accept` hanging); dropping the listener aborts those tasks. New `BitwardenSSHAgent::start_on(&str)` (via `SSHAgentServer::start_on_pipe`, `create_listeners_on`) starts the agent on a given pipe name; the 21 `server_windows.rs` tests use a unique name each, with a client open that asks only for the rights the DACL grants (tokio's `ClientOptions` asks for `GENERIC_WRITE`, which is refused), and the new `ssh_add_windows.rs` runs the runner's real `ssh-add.exe -l` against an empty agent. `Win32_Storage_FileSystem` is added to the `windows` features for the test client open. A name that is already taken (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` or `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY` on the first instance) returns the typed `PipeNameTaken { name }`, re-exported on Windows from `lib.rs`, `server/mod.rs` and `listener/mod.rs`, so `crates/ssh` can tell the user to disable the OpenSSH service or close the other owner. The two tests that created the pipe name twice now go through the listener. `WindowsListener::with_name` lets tests bind to a unique pipe name so they don't collide with the runner's OpenSSH agent service on `PIPE_NAME`. `Cargo.toml` adds `windows` features `Win32_Security`, `Win32_Security_Authorization`, `Win32_System_Threading`. | Upstream creates unrestricted instances on demand, so a same-user process (or the OpenSSH agent service) can squat the name or add an instance and steal the next client. The DACL withholds `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE`, which is why instances are pooled and reused. Resets are retried with backoff before an instance is given up; a lost instance is logged at error level with the remaining count, and `accept` fails once none is left. The drain/recycle tasks live in the same `JoinSet` as the armed ones, so dropping the listener aborts them all and closes queued instances; a bind that hits the name-taken error retries for 500 ms so a just-dropped listener's instances can finish closing (disable then enable in one process). |
| `Cargo.toml` | `zeroize = "1.9.1"` added; tokio gains the `time` feature (it only compiled through feature unification before); the dev-dependency tokio gains `test-util`. | Wiping key copies; read deadlines and accept backoff; paused-clock tests for the deadlines. |
| `src/agent.rs` | New `epoch: Mutex<u64>` (values drawn from a process-wide counter, so an epoch never matches another agent instance), `BitwardenSSHAgent::epoch()` and `replace_if(epoch, keys) -> Result<bool>`. `clear()` and `stop()` clear the keystore and bump the epoch under the lock; `replace` and `replace_if` hold it too. Tests `replace_if_with_the_current_epoch_replaces`, `replace_if_after_a_clear_discards_the_keys`, `replace_if_after_a_stop_discards_the_keys`, `an_epoch_from_another_agent_never_matches`. | A key refresh that started before a vault lock could finish after it and serve the keys again; the compare and the replace have to be atomic with the clear. |
| `src/storage/serialization.rs` | `SSHKeyDataSerializable` zeroizes `private_key` on drop (fields are moved out with `mem::take`). New `to_zeroizing_bytes` serializes into an `AlignedVec` pre-sized to the entry plus `SERIALIZATION_HEADROOM`, copies it into a `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` and wipes the buffer; the PEM stays in `Zeroizing` until it moves into the struct. `TryFrom<Vec<u8>> for SSHKeyData` wipes its input; `TryFrom<PrivateKey> for String` and `TryFrom<SSHKeyData> for Vec<u8>` keep their signatures over the same helpers. New test `serializing_an_rsa_key_never_reallocates_the_buffer`. | Every replace, list and sign left plaintext private keys in freed memory (the PEM `String`, rkyv's growing buffer, the intermediate `Vec`s and the deserialized struct). |
| `src/storage/keystore.rs` | The store, a plaintext `BTreeMap<PublicKey, name>` and `initialized` sit under one `Mutex<Inner>`. `get_all_public_keys_and_names` reads the names map (no decryption); `insert`/`replace` hand `Zeroizing` bytes to the store; a decryption failure (the store re-keyed and dropped everything) also clears the names and `initialized`. | A list decrypted and parsed every private key; `replace` set `initialized` after releasing the store lock, so a racing `clear` left an empty but initialized store, and the tamper path kept `initialized`, both making `ssh-add -l` answer an empty list with no unlock prompt. |
| `src/server/connection.rs` | The stream is wrapped in a `BufReader`. Waiting for a request has `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (15 min); once a request's first byte arrived, the length and body must follow within `MESSAGE_TIMEOUT` (10 s). A non-extension request is raced against the cancellation token and the client closing (`fill_buf` returning EOF); buffered data from a pipelined request ends the watch and stays for the next read. An `ssh-rsa` sign request without SHA-2 flags is refused before `authorize`. The upstream test `sign_request_rsa_without_flags_returns_failure` now expects `get_private_key` never and checks the policy was not asked; new tests `idle_connection_is_closed_after_the_idle_timeout`, `stalled_request_is_closed_after_the_message_timeout`, `client_closing_while_approval_is_pending_drops_the_request`, `pipelined_request_is_not_mistaken_for_a_close`. | A stalled client pinned a task, a descriptor and up to 256 KiB forever (on Windows four of them hold the whole pipe pool); a client that quit left the approval prompt up and an approval signed for nobody; SHA-1 RSA requests were refused only after the user approved them. |
| `src/server/mod.rs` | The accept loop takes a permit from a `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS` (64) semaphore before dispatching a connection; the handler task holds it. `is_running()` is also `false` once the accept loop has finished (every listener exited); `start` cancels the stale token of such a server. Tests `exhausted_listener_stops_the_server`, `failing_accept_backs_off_and_keeps_running`. | Unbounded concurrent Unix connections; a dead listener was reported as running. |
| `src/server/listener/mod.rs` | The listener task body moves to `run_listener`; failed accepts back off from `ACCEPT_BACKOFF_MIN` (10 ms) doubling to `ACCEPT_BACKOFF_MAX` (1 s), reset after a success; a `ListenerExhausted` error ends the task. | A failing `accept` (Windows pool exhausted, Unix `EMFILE`) was retried immediately in a loop: 100% CPU and a log flood. |
| `src/server/listener/windows.rs` | `pool_exhausted()` returns `ListenerExhausted`. The 20 ms pause of the rebind loop (`REBIND_POLL`) runs in `block_in_place` on a multi-thread runtime and as a plain sleep otherwise. | Exhaustion is permanent, so the listener stops instead of spinning; the bind is synchronous on a runtime thread. |
| `src/server/session_bind.rs` | ECDSA host keys (nistp256/384/521) are verified with ssh-key's `EcdsaPublicKey` verifier; the signature algorithm must match the host key. Tests `valid_ecdsa_signature_binds_the_host`, `ecdsa_signature_by_another_key_is_rejected`, `ecdsa_signature_over_another_session_is_rejected`. | Upstream rejected every ECDSA session-bind, so `ssh -A` to a host with an ECDSA key left `is_forwarding` unset and forwarded sign requests looked like local ones in the approval prompt. |

## secure_memory

| File | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/secure_key/mod.rs`, `src/lib.rs` | New public `Backend` enum with `name()`, `backend()` (creates a key and reports its container) and the private `CrossPlatformSecureKeyContainer::backend`, plus the test `backend_names_the_platform_mechanism`. | The Linux security status shows which link of the key-in-memory chain is active (memfd_secret, keyctl or mlock); upstream only logs it. `mseal` of the memfd_secret mapping (linux-plan.md 1e) is not added: the container unmaps the page on drop, and a sealed mapping cannot be unmapped. |
| `Cargo.toml` | `zeroize = "1.9.1"` added. | Wiping key copies. |
| `src/secure_key/crypto.rs`, `mlock.rs`, `memfd_secret.rs`, `dpapi.rs` | The generated key in `MemoryEncryptionKey::new` and DPAPI's decrypted and padded buffers are `Zeroizing`; `as_key` converts the slice with `<&[u8; KEY_SIZE]>::try_from` instead of copying it into a by-value array. | Stack copies of the memory-encryption key were never wiped. |
| `src/encrypted_memory_store.rs` | `to_vec` wipes the values it already decrypted when a later one fails. | They were dropped unwiped on the error path. |
